metadata.title: Loan Eligibility System Comparison Scorecard
metadata.caveat: Illustrative policy values (D-02). Not a performance ranking; reflects architectural design properties.

transparency.name: Transparency
transparency.question: Can a person see why this decision was made?

auditability.name: Auditability
auditability.question: Can a decision be reconstructed and checked later?

edge_cases.name: Edge Cases
edge_cases.question: Does it behave sensibly where inputs are odd?

regulatory_defensibility.name: Regulatory Defensibility
regulatory_defensibility.question: Could this be defended against the framework in docs/regulatory-mapping.md?

transparency.anchor: Every decision lists the rules that fired and the facts they used, and the applicant-facing reasons are exactly the reason codes of those rules (tested on all of D1).
transparency.justification: Every decision generates an exact trace containing only fired rules, with adverse notices rendered verbatim from reason code definitions in rules/reason_codes.toml.

auditability.anchor: A stored record per decision, a version for the logic used, and a replay that reproduces the decision and trace, with a mismatch reported when a parameter changes.
auditability.justification: Every decision is committed to an append-only SQLite audit log with input SHA-256 and ruleset hash, verifiable via byte-identical replay.

edge_cases.anchor: No unexplained difference in any category; every missing-data and boundary case ends in a stated outcome.
edge_cases.justification: Evaluated on 64 edge cases across 5 categories with 61 exact catalog matches, 3 explained FOIR-capacity interactions (OQ-012), and zero unexplained differences.

regulatory_defensibility.anchor: All six rows met with evidence.
regulatory_defensibility.justification: Fully satisfies requirements CR-01 to CR-06 with verifiable tests for specific reason notices, KFS summaries, consent enforcement, and human referral.

transparency.anchor: Each decision has an exact, per-decision explanation from the model's own arithmetic (the logistic regression's feature contributions), but the explanation is a score contribution, not a policy reason the applicant can act on.
transparency.justification: Linear feature contributions provide exact additive logit shifts per applicant, but output numerical score weights rather than actionable policy clauses.

auditability.anchor: Versioned artifact and seed, and the numbers reproduce, but no per-decision record or replay.
auditability.justification: Model training reproduces deterministically from derived seed with recorded dataset and split hashes, but lacks an append-only decision audit store and replay capability.

edge_cases.anchor: An unexplained difference in the missing-data or boundary categories.
edge_cases.justification: Silently imputes missing mandatory data with median training values without schema validation, and smoothly crosses policy thresholds without discrete bounds.

regulatory_defensibility.anchor: Two or three rows partly met or gaps.
regulatory_defensibility.justification: Meets CR-05 (model card) and CR-06 (bias testing), but leaves gaps on CR-01 (actionable specific adverse reasons), CR-02 (KFS offer terms), and CR-04 (human referral).

transparency.anchor: Only a global explanation exists (permutation importance), not one per decision.
transparency.justification: Provides global tree feature importances only; non-linear ensemble interactions lack exact closed-form per-decision explanations without complex local approximations.

auditability.anchor: Versioned artifact and seed, and the numbers reproduce, but no per-decision record or replay.
auditability.justification: Reproducible training pipeline from fixed seed and versioned split hashes, without individual decision tracing or replay store.

edge_cases.anchor: An unexplained difference in the missing-data or boundary categories.
edge_cases.justification: Imputes missing values without error flagging and produces continuous prediction manifolds across hard policy thresholds.

regulatory_defensibility.anchor: Two or three rows partly met or gaps.
regulatory_defensibility.justification: Meets CR-05 and CR-06, but cannot provide per-decision adverse reasons (CR-01), loan terms (CR-02), or human review routing (CR-04).

d2_test.population_note: Test split (N = 46,127). The rule system approves 1.68% (776 applicants) due to severe mapping constraints (K04, K05, unknown delinquency).

d3_test.population_note: Synthetic test split (N = 3,000). Agreement with policy is partly circular because D3 labels derive from simulated credit policy rules.
